events.description: An engineer starts setting up multiple PostgreSQL servers in the staging environment to try out pgpool-II for load balancing queries (infrastructure#259).
Prior to starting this work, the engineer takes an LVM snapshot of the production database and loads it into the staging environment, outside the normal automatic 01:00 UTC schedule.

GitLab.com starts experiencing a significant increase in database load, suspected to be spam; many users are unable to post comments on issues and merge requests, and getting load under control takes several hours.
Part of the load is traced to a background job trying to remove a GitLab employee's account and associated data, which was accidentally scheduled for removal after being flagged for abuse.

Due to increased load, PostgreSQL secondary replication lags and fails because WAL segments were already removed from the primary; with no WAL archiving, the secondary must be manually re-synchronised.
pg_basebackup hangs without meaningful output; after several tries it reports the master lacks available replication connections, so max_wal_senders is temporarily raised from 3 to 32.
PostgreSQL refuses to restart due to too many semaphores; max_connections (set to 8000) is reduced to 2000, and PostgreSQL restarts successfully.
pg_basebackup still does not start replication immediately; strace shows it hanging in a poll call with no further useful information.

An engineer suspects pg_basebackup created files in the secondary's data directory during previous attempts; this is later revealed to be normal behaviour, which was not documented in runbooks or official documentation.

While trying to restore replication, an engineer wipes the PostgreSQL data directory believing it is the secondary, but it is the primary; the process is terminated a second or two later, but around 300 GB of data has already been removed.
Engineers look for database backups and ask for help on Slack; the process of finding and using backups fails completely.

The pg_dump backups are found to be missing: the S3 bucket is empty because the backup used pg_dump 9.2 against a PostgreSQL 9.6 database, causing the backup to fail; cronjob failure emails were rejected due to DMARC not being enabled, so the failure went unnoticed.
Azure disk snapshots are found to be disabled for database servers, as they were assumed unnecessary given other backup procedures.

events.time: February 1st ~17:00 UTC (approx. 18 hours of copying after decision)
events.description: The GitLab.com database is restored without webhooks; the restoration used the LVM snapshot from ~6 hours before the outage, after copying data from staging to production took around 18 hours due to slow disks.
Final restoration procedures are completed, including restoring webhooks and confirming everything operates as expected.
The database is restored to the state it was at January 31st 17:20 UTC; data created between January 31st 17:20 UTC and 23:30 UTC is lost.
